subtype: Approach: postponing the discussion because it feels uncomfortable [Pitfall]
passage: Thursday night. Over dinner Kunal said, "So... are we ever having a baby?" and I nearly dropped my spoon. For two years I assumed we both meant "later". I never asked because it felt awkward, like touching something that might break. Turns out Kunal has been thinking of next year, and I have been thinking of five years from now, when the promotion has settled. We talked until the dal went cold. Kunal is worried about waiting too long and I am worried about money and time, and neither of us knew the other was carrying it. I wish we had spoken before it piled up. Relieved it's out, and a bit foolish. Going to set a time to talk properly on Sunday, with tea. - Bhupen

qa.q: What did Kunal ask over dinner?
qa.a: Kunal asked, "So... are we ever having a baby?"

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling at the end of the diary entry?
qa.a: Bhupen felt relieved that it was out in the open, and a bit foolish for waiting so long.

qa.q: What could Bhupen and Kunal do at the Sunday talk?
qa.a: They could each share their timeline and worries, listen fully, and look for a plan they both accept without rushing.

qa.q: How might Kunal have felt during the two years?
qa.a: Kunal was probably carrying the worry about waiting too long alone, and may have wondered whether Bhupen felt the same.

grounding: Bhupen and Kunal each assume the other agrees, and discover different timelines after two years of avoiding the talk.
